case_name: Susmita Chandran vs. Avantika Ray — CT Case No.1581/2020
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties had a domestic violence case filed under the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act. The matter was referred to mediation and an amicable settlement was reached.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can settle disputes and agree to withdraw cases.
legal_principles.held: The parties shall file a joint application for waiving of statutory period of six months within 15 days from the date of filing of joint petition under Section 13-B(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can agree to quash FIRs and criminal proceedings.
legal_principles.held: The parties shall file petition under Section 482 Cr. P.C. for quashing of FIR / CR Case No. 234/2017 within 30 days after the petition Under Section 13B (1) Hindu Marriage Act is allowed by the Hon'ble Family Court at Nagpur.

outcome.final_order: The parties agreed to dissolve their marriage by mutual consent, with the husband returning two locked bags and paying a sum of Rs.7,50,000/- to the wife.
